Okay, so I'm trying to figure out which immune system function is carried out by antibodies. The options are A, B, C, D. Let me start by recalling what I know about antibodies from my biology classes. 

I remember that antibodies are produced by the immune system in response to an antigen, like a virus or bacteria. They're kind of like the immune system's way of recognizing and fighting off invaders. So, what exactly do they do? I think they have something to do with marking the invaders so the immune system can deal with them. Maybe that's one function.

Option A says antibodies produce proteins that attach to an invading virus. Wait, don't antibodies themselves attach to the virus, not produce the proteins. The proteins might be something else, like cytokines or something. So A might be incorrect.

Option B says antibodies attach to an invading virus as a target marker. That sounds familiar. I think once an antibody binds to the virus, it signals the immune system to take action, like using other cells to engulf or destroy the virus. So B seems right.

Option C says antibodies engulf the virus. I think that's more of the job of white blood cells, like macrophages or neutrophils, which engulf pathogens. Antibodies might help by marking them, but not engulfing themselves. So C might not be correct.

Option D says antibodies release enzymes that lyse the virus. I'm not sure about that. I thought lysing enzymes might be produced by other cells, maybe in combination with antibodies. So D might not be the primary function.

Putting it all together, the main function is that antibodies attach to the virus as a marker. So the correct answer is B.
